page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of a bundled 2500 GB NVMe SSD. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates polarized performance characteristics. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2314.0, which falls in the top 10%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression register strong results in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is comparatively limited, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. Memory read bandwidth is also relatively low, though large-block write bandwidth and database operations maintain average performance levels.

From a resource density perspective, the i7ie.xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive local storage and memory capacity without needing high parallel compute power. This allows users to avoid paying for excess vCPUs to obtain substantial storage and RAM. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core scaling and memory read throughput. This profile is appropriate for relational databases, NoSQL databases, text processing, and single-threaded data compression pipelines.
